From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ari Murphy <ari.murphy@optihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — license model & token bands (quote calibration)

Hi Ari — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can pull together a calibrated private/VPC quote.

Key notes from our discovery call:
- Usage profile: 3 production environments (prod, staging, dev) + 2 training/sandbox; peak typical concurrency small (5–10 rps) but monthly token volume expected to be spiky.
- Token volumes: baseline ~120M tokens/month with occasional bursts to ~400M in month‑end processing batches.
- Critical requirements: VPC peering, customer KMS, 90‑day audit log retention (SOC2 evidence required), and a 99.9% availability target for prod.

Pricing calibration asks (best if you can confirm by EOD Mon):
1) Target unit econ: what dollar target do you have for $/1M tokens once Private is in place (ballpark is fine)?
2) Budget range: is there a monthly committed budget range we should anchor to for reserved capacity (e.g., $50k–$150k/month)?
3) Environment mapping: confirm that you want three production-like envs + two sandboxes (we'll price envs differently if you want fewer).

What we'll deliver after we get the above: a 2–option quote (Committed Reserved + Burst plan) and an Order Form draft showing licensing fee, per‑1M token unit price, and included support tier. I'll also include an early token‑econ model so you can see effective $/1M at different monthly commits (attached: token_econ_model.xlsx (stub)).

Attachments: token_econ_model.xlsx (stub)

Next steps: if you can reply with the three bullets above, I can get a formal proposal and Order Form to you by Wed (48 hours). If you'd prefer, we can also schedule a quick 20‑minute follow-up to walk the economics.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment — license model & token bands (quote calibration)

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. Answers inline below.

On Sat, Apr 11, 2026 at 4:12 PM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Key notes from our discovery call:
> - Usage profile: 3 production environments (prod, staging, dev) + 2 training/sandbox; peak typical concurrency small (5–10 rps) but monthly token volume expected to be spiky.
> - Token volumes: baseline ~120M tokens/month with occasional bursts to ~400M in month‑end processing batches.
> - Critical requirements: VPC peering, customer KMS, 90‑day audit log retention (SOC2 evidence required), and a 99.9% availability target for prod.

Confirm: that env split is correct — prod/staging/dev + 2 sandboxes.

On pricing calibration asks:
1) Target unit econ: Our finance lead is pushing for a target of ~$800 per 1M tokens net (after discounts) for committed usage. If that's unrealistic for private, flag it and propose the closest bands.
2) Budget range: We can commit roughly $40k–$120k/month depending on how licensing is structured (flat licensing fee vs per‑token). If you offer a hybrid (small base license + discounted units), that would be preferred.
3) Environment mapping: Confirmed as above.

Other asks: Can you confirm what support tiers include (response SLAs, number of named contacts, on‑call coverage)? Also need to know whether the license fee covers unlimited model upgrades/patches or whether those are billed separately.

We need the formal proposal by Wed if possible — procurement has an internal window to discuss next week.

Best,
Ari
VP Product, OptiHealth
ari.murphy@optihealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Ari / OptiHealth — budget + support questions (need quote options)

Looping you in — forwarding Ari's reply. Quick notes:
- Ari's target $/1M of ~$800 is aggressive for an on‑prem/private deployment unless we push reserved capacity and longer term commit (12–24 months). For private we should present:
  Option A (Committed Reserved): 12‑month term, base license (covers runtime + control plane) + per‑1M token at $950 with volume tiers that drop to $700 at >1B tokens/month.
  Option B (Hybrid Reservation): Lower base license + higher per‑1M ($1,100) but with a monthly reserved commit floor and burst billing at a lower incremental rate.
- Support: propose "Enterprise" tier (24/7 critical on‑call, 2‑hour P1 response, 8x5 P2) as default for OptiHealth; price as an uplift (percentage of license or flat monthly). We should include a "Business" tier alternative (M‑F oncall, 4‑hour P1, 24‑hour P2).
- Env pricing: price prod envs at full license footprint, charge sandboxes at a discounted flat fee each (e.g., 20% of prod env license).

Rishi — can you confirm the capacity assumptions (GPU footprint, expected node counts) for the three prod envs + sandboxes? Also confirm whether we can support 90‑day audit log retention in their VPC config (IIRC yes, but need to confirm retention storage cost).

I'll draft the two options and a one‑page comparison for Soojin to send to OptiHealth.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

What you'll see from us by EOD Wed:
- Option A: Committed Reserved (12‑month) — base license + tiered per‑1M pricing. This will be the lower effective $/1M at scale (we'll show breakpoints at 100M, 500M, 1B tokens).
- Option B: Hybrid Reservation — lower upfront license, higher unit price, flexible burst.
- Support addenda: one‑page comparison (Business vs Enterprise) with SLAs and named response times.
- Order Form draft (attached) showing fees, term, and environment mapping; we'll mark optional items (additional sandboxes, extended log retention) so procurement can toggle.

Attachments included: Redwood_Private_OrderForm_v1.pdf (stub), token_econ_model.xlsx (stub)

1) I will send the full PDF Order Form + price table by Wed morning.

If anything changes on your side (especially commit band), reply here and we'll re‑calibrate.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.
